whatWasMissing.note: The model could bail out (applyBailoutIntent, via InputIntent.bailout) but had no setpoint operation, and the client set neither: a CCR dive started at the configured setpoint and stayed there, and the only way to bail out was a save edited by hand. Nothing in the HUD showed the loop — setpoint, PO₂, cylinders, scrubber — so #158's e2e tests read localStorage to learn what a CCR dive had started with, and the gas row showed tanks[0], the codec's placeholder cylinder.
whatWasMissing.consequence: The rebreather was configurable and simulated but not operable, and its state was observable only through the save.

deliberateDesign.operationsAreTheModels: The controller passes a delta or a request; DiveModel decides. No rebreather, on bailout, failed, at a bound, or a non-finite delta all return the same state reference, and the controller then publishes nothing and saves nothing — the same silence as a refused gas switch. There is one place for each rule.
deliberateDesign.irreversibleByConstruction: No operation clears onBailout. A second bailOut() returns the same reference and adds no event; the intent path through advance() already behaved this way and is untouched. Confirmed by state rather than by a dialog (#67): the row that held the button is gone, the cylinder row names the diluent, and the keys stop being claimed.
deliberateDesign.keysClaimedOnlyWhenOnOffer: `[` `]` and B call preventDefault() only under #loopControlsOffered(), the same rule as the digits and F: a key that does nothing is left to whoever else wants it.
deliberateDesign.rowsSwap: On a CCR dive the five loop rows show and the open-circuit gas row hides, rather than both showing. The gas row on a CCR dive would read tanks[0]'s pressure, a cylinder nobody draws down; showing it beside the O₂ and diluent rows would be a third pressure with no meaning.
deliberateDesign.twoDecimalsForPo2: formatPartialPressure gives two decimals for setpoint and loop PO₂ (legacy: toFixed(1) for SP, toFixed(2) for PO2). A loop at 1.28 and one at 1.32 are different readings; a cylinder to the tenth of a bar is already more than anyone reads.
deliberateDesign.warningPrecedence: failure > scrubberLow > co2 > oxygen > lowGas, which is the legacy banner's effective order (see boundsPortedFromTheOracle.warnings). The first cut ranked PO₂ above the scrubber on the argument that a hyperoxic loop is more urgent than nine minutes of scrubber; review round 1 held that docs/decisions.md makes the legacy harness the behavioural oracle and that a re-ranking needs its own committed decision. Accepted: the oracle's order stands until such a decision exists.
deliberateDesign.lowGasOnTheBreathedCylinder: Low gas fires on the active cylinder for open circuit, on the diluent after a bailout, and never on the loop — the loop is not a cylinder, and tanks[0] there is the placeholder. Before this slice the rule read tanks[0] on a CCR dive too; at 200 bar it never fired, so nothing observable changes, but the rule now says what it means.
deliberateDesign.bailoutNameCarriesTheConsequence: The bailout button's accessible name is 'Bail out to open circuit — cannot be undone'. It cannot ask for confirmation (#67), so its irreversibility has to be knowable before the press rather than discovered after it.
deliberateDesign.hiddenRowsNeedCss: `.wreck-hud div` sets display: flex, which beats the user agent's [hidden] rule; `.wreck-hud div[hidden] { display: none }` was added so the loop rows actually vanish on open circuit. Asserted by the e2e that checks the rows hidden.
deliberateDesign.forcedForecastSurvivesAFlight: A forced forecast (gas switch, setpoint, bailout) that arrives while a request is in flight is remembered; the in-flight answer, computed for the gas the diver has left, is not published, and one replacement goes out from the latest state when it settles. Several forces during one flight collapse into that one replacement.

sliceBoundary.issueSuggestion: #163 proposes 'PR 3: CCR setpoint + bailout'. This is that PR, plus the HUD rows and warnings the issue lists under 'HUD additions the controls need' for the loop, because a setpoint control without a setpoint readout cannot be tested through the HUD.
sliceBoundary.stillOutstandingInThisIssue: gas info (I); the parity trace with a tank switch, a setpoint change and a bailout — the baseline fixture has a tank switch (trimix-45m-20min) and a bailout (ccr-bailout-30m) but no setpoint change, so a scenario has to be recorded from the legacy client and the fixture regenerated additively; the switchDepth decision carried over from #158; bailout as a status-chip state (legacy's BAIL mode word in danger tone) if the cylinder row is judged insufficient.

notTestedAndWhy.audioCue: Each new severity drives audio.update({ warningActive: true }), the same path the three existing severities use, which plays alert.warning at priority 100 through WebAudioService. The node test environment has no AudioContext and the e2e cannot hear; the mapping is one boolean derived from the same selectWarning() the alert text comes from, so the visual assertion covers the branch.
notTestedAndWhy.loopPo2Warning: LOW PO2 / HIGH PO2 on the loop: reaching 0.18 or 1.5 bar takes a starved or runaway loop that the save codec accepts but that fails the dive within 30 s of resuming, so an e2e would race the failure. The branch is the same `oxygen` severity the open-circuit path already asserts (tests/wreck-slice.spec.js 'persisted safety states'), with the thresholds substituted.
notTestedAndWhy.saveThrottle: The app writes a save every five simulated seconds, so the e2e reads that follow a second press wait for a save that reflects it (savedStateWhere) rather than asserting the first save they find. That is an ordering in the app, not a defect; a save on every discrete act would be a separate decision.

bailoutForecastGas.finding: major bug — after a bailout, bestForecastGas() scans state.tanks for ascent steps and stops and can pick tanks[0], the codec's placeholder cylinder, which the diver cannot breathe.
bailoutForecastGas.assessment: Disputed as a finding against this PR. It is the oracle's behaviour: src/physics.js calculateDecoSchedule uses activeGas() (the diluent on bailout) for the current segment but bestGasForDepth(d) for every ascent step and stop, and outside tec mode that returns tanks[activeTank] — the placeholder. The migration planner reproduces it, and it predates this PR, which adds bailOut() and calls the same forced forecast a gas switch already called.
bailoutForecastGas.disposition: Tracked as #183: a normative decision, the planner change, and a baseline scenario whose diluent differs from the placeholder cylinder (ccr-bailout-30m uses air for both and cannot tell them apart). Answered on the PR.

forcedForecastDropped.finding: minor bug — #requestForecast(true) returned at the pending guard, so a force during a periodic request was lost and the stale answer was published.
forcedForecastDropped.fix: #forcedForecastQueued: the stale answer is dropped and a replacement issued from the latest state on settle. Three unit tests in tests/unit/game-controller-forecast.test.ts drive the worker client by hand.

warningPrecedence.finding: major contract-violation — PO₂ ranked above SCR LOW, diverging from the legacy banner without a committed decision.
warningPrecedence.fix: selectWarning() now follows SCR LOW > CO2! > PO2.

supersedes.why: Predates review round 1, which found the forced forecast lost during a flight and the warning precedence diverging from the oracle.
